modules.title: Company Orientation and 1 related area
modules.purpose: To orient new employees to Aurelle Hotels & Residences company policies, code of conduct, handbook guidelines, and initial role-specific requirements.
assessment_topics: Company Orientation and Code of Conduct
modules.completion_criteria: Complete all checklist items, tasks, and scenarios, and score at least 80% on the quiz.

content.text: Understand and apply the employee handbook guidelines, identification procedures, and attendance recording rules.
Comply with the Code of Workplace Conduct regarding declarations, harassment prohibition, gift limits, and uniform standards.
Navigate grievance escalation, media enquiry protocols, and F&B daily service responsibilities.

content.activity: Sign the Code of Conduct declaration before the first shift.
Read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form on the first working day.
Collect staff ID badge from Human Resources and wear it visibly at all times.
Complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path within the first 30 days.

content.description: Review daily menu, specials, and allergen information with your supervisor prior to your shift.
content.expected_outcome: Complete command of food offerings and dietary accommodations before service starts.
content.completion_criteria: Successfully brief the supervisor on daily specials and allergen requirements.

content.situation: A guest offers you a complimentary gift valued at USD 30 as a token of appreciation for great service.
expected_actions: Recognize that gifts above USD 25 must be declared.
Declare the gift to the Duty Manager within 24 hours.

content.question: All employees must sign the Code of Conduct declaration before their first shift.
content.explanation: All employees must sign the Code of Conduct declaration before their first shift.

content.question: What is the maximum value of unsolicited gifts from guests an employee may accept without declaring it?
content.explanation: Employees may accept unsolicited gifts from guests up to a value of USD 25; any gift above this value must be declared to the Duty Manager within 24 hours.

options: Answer their questions truthfully if you were present.
Refer all enquiries to the Communications team and do not speak to the media.
Ask your direct supervisor to handle the interview on the spot.
Direct them to Human Resources immediately.
content.question: What should you do if a journalist approaches you with media enquiries about an incident at the hotel?
content.explanation: Employees must not speak to the media about any incident and must refer all enquiries to the Communications team.

options: Sign a paper timesheet at the front desk
Text your supervisor when you arrive
Use the staff entrance and record attendance on the biometric clock at the start and end of every shift
Clock in via your personal mobile phone application
content.question: How should attendance be recorded for every shift?
content.explanation: Employees must use the staff entrance and record attendance on the biometric clock at the start and end of every shift.

content.question: If a grievance remains unresolved with your direct supervisor after how many working days should it be escalated in writing to Human Resources?
content.explanation: Grievances must be raised first with the direct supervisor and, if unresolved within five working days, escalated in writing to Human Resources.

content.question: Where should team members take their breaks during shifts?
content.explanation: Please remind your teams to take their breaks away from guest areas.

content.topic: Company Orientation and Code of Conduct

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly answers policy questions and completes handbook acknowledgement tasks.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates full understanding of attendance rules, ID requirements, and signing the employee handbook on Day 1.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately resolves the gift declaration scenario and conducts compliance checks.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly identifies gift limits, harassment policies, and uniform standards.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly follows escalation guidelines and F&B menu knowledge standards.
rubric.expected_performance: Applies correct grievance escalation timelines and media referral protocols.

modules.title: Data Privacy
modules.purpose: To ensure F&B Associates at Aurelle Penang Heritage handle guest and employee personal data in strict compliance with data privacy policies, protection regulations, and security standards.
key_concepts: Prohibition of personal devices for guest data
modules.completion_criteria: Completion of all checklist items, tasks, scenarios, and achieving a passing score on the quiz and knowledge assessment.

content.text: Identify permitted access conditions for guest personal data and adhere to purpose limitation rules.
Recognize prohibited actions regarding identity document scanning, retention, and the prohibition of personal mobile phone use.
Explain the reporting procedures for data incidents and data handling rules for Malaysian properties and personnel files.

content.description: Review the data handling policies for Aurelle Penang Heritage regarding guest identity documents, PMS scanning, and mobile device restrictions.
content.expected_outcome: Understand that guest identity documents may only be scanned into the PMS, must be deleted after 7 days, and must never touch personal mobile devices or messaging apps.
content.completion_criteria: Acknowledge in writing that personal mobile devices will never be used to receive, photograph, or store guest identity documents.

content.situation: A caller phones the F&B outlet asking if a specific guest is staying at Aurelle Penang Heritage and requests their room number.
expected_actions: Refuse to disclose the room number or guest name to the caller.
Connect the call to the room without confirming the guest's presence.

content.question: Within what timeframe must Guest Data Privacy training be completed?
content.explanation: Guest Data Privacy training must be completed within Week 1.

content.question: Guest personal data may be accessed whenever an employee is curious about a guest.
content.explanation: Guest personal data may only be accessed to deliver the guest's stay or for a documented business need.

options: Paper copies kept at the front desk
content.question: Where are scanned copies of guest identity documents permitted to be stored?
content.explanation: A guest's passport or national ID may be scanned only into the PMS; paper copies are prohibited.

options: No later than 3 days after check-out
No later than 7 days after check-out
At the end of the calendar year
content.question: When must scanned copies of guest identity documents be permanently deleted from the PMS?
content.explanation: Scanned copies of guest identity documents must be permanently deleted from the PMS no later than 7 days after check-out.

options: Confirm the guest is staying and provide the room number
Refuse to talk to the caller entirely
Connect the call to the room without confirming the guest's presence
Ask the caller for their ID before disclosing details
content.question: What is the correct procedure when a caller asks for a guest's room number?
content.explanation: Room numbers and guest names must not be disclosed to callers or visitors; calls are to be connected to the room without confirming the guest's presence.

options: By the end of the week
content.question: Within what timeframe must any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data be reported to the Duty Manager and IT?
content.explanation: Any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data must be reported to the Duty Manager and IT within 1 hour of discovery.

rubric.pass_condition: Answers all access-related questions and scenarios correctly.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates full comprehension that data access is restricted to delivery of stay or documented business needs.

rubric.criterion: Prohibition of Personal Devices and Unapproved Storage
rubric.pass_condition: Passes tasks and multiple-choice questions regarding scanning, PMS retention limits, and mobile phone prohibitions.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly identifies that identity documents must never be stored on personal phones or USB drives.

rubric.pass_condition: Identifies the correct 1-hour reporting window and proper caller routing protocol.
rubric.expected_performance: Knows to report suspected data loss within 1 hour and how to handle caller inquiries.

modules.title: Fire & Life Safety and 1 related area
modules.purpose: To equip new employees with essential fire safety, emergency response, and health and safety procedures at Aurelle Hotels & Residences.
assessment_topics: Fire & Life Safety and Health & Safety Standards
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all Day 1 and Week 1 checklist items, tasks, and pass the knowledge assessment.

content.text: Identify fire assembly points, evacuation routes, and execute the RACE procedure during emergencies.
Apply proper health, safety, and PPE standards for chemical handling, lifting heavy loads, and uniform maintenance.

content.activity: Attend fire and life safety orientation on Day 1
Locate the fire assembly point and the two nearest fire exits for the work area
Complete Chemical Handling training before first use of cleaning or pool chemicals

content.description: Identify and document the location of your work area's fire assembly point and the two nearest fire exits.
content.expected_outcome: A confirmed understanding of emergency evacuation routes specific to your work location.
content.completion_criteria: Submit the exact locations of the assembly point and two nearest fire exits to your supervisor.

content.situation: You hear the fire alarm sound while working in your area. You need to evacuate and notice a coworker attempting to use the guest elevator to speed up their exit.
expected_actions: Follow the RACE procedure (Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Evacuate).
Prevent your coworker from using the lifts, as lifts must not be used.
Proceed immediately to the designated fire assembly point.

content.question: Fire and Life Safety orientation must be completed on Day 1.
content.explanation: Fire and Life Safety orientation must be completed on Day 1.

options: A fire and life safety orientation
content.question: What must every new employee attend on their first day regarding fire safety?
content.explanation: Every new employee must attend a fire and life safety orientation on their first day.

content.question: What does the acronym RACE stand for when following emergency procedures upon hearing the fire alarm?
content.explanation: On hearing the fire alarm, employees must follow the RACE procedure (Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Evacuate) and must not use the lifts.

content.question: How often must all employees participate in a fire drill?
content.explanation: All employees must participate in a fire drill every six months.

content.question: What protective items must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools? (Select all that apply)
content.explanation: Safety footwear, gloves and eye protection must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools.

options: They must be lifted quickly by a single person.
They must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley.
They can be moved by one person if wearing safety footwear.
content.question: What is the requirement for handling loads heavier than 20 kg?
content.explanation: Loads heavier than 20 kg must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley.

content.topic: Fire & Life Safety and Health & Safety Standards

rubric.criterion: Understanding of Emergency and Safety Procedures
rubric.pass_condition: Achieves 100% accuracy on knowledge assessment.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates accurate knowledge of orientation requirements, RACE procedures, assembly points, PPE usage, and heavy lifting limits.

modules.title: Food Safety and 3 related areas
modules.purpose: To equip F&B associates and staff with foundational knowledge in food safety, guest service recovery, finance, and IT procedures to ensure high standards of safety, compliance, and guest satisfaction.
key_concepts: Chilled and hot food temperature requirements
Incident logging and sensitive complaint escalation
modules.completion_criteria: Complete all reading activities, tasks, scenarios, and achieve a passing score on the module quiz.

content.text: Apply essential food safety standards including temperature controls, allergen procedures, and illness reporting.
Handle guest complaints properly using the CARE model, timely logging, and correct escalation criteria.
Understand general operational requirements regarding finance reconciliation, expense submissions, IT apps, and FAQs.

content.activity: Complete Food Safety Level 1 training before handling open food

content.description: Submit a practice expense claim submission timeline check following company rules.
content.expected_outcome: Demonstrate understanding of expense claim deadlines and requirements.
content.completion_criteria: State that expense claims must be submitted with original receipts within 30 days of the expense.

content.situation: A guest declares a severe nut allergy while ordering food in the restaurant. You need to ensure their safety according to hotel policy.
expected_actions: Check the Allergen Matrix for every dish ordered.
Inform the chef in person about the declared allergy.
Ensure the kitchen ticket is marked with a purple allergy flag.
Serve the allergy-declared order yourself as the server who took the order.

content.question: What is the maximum required storage temperature for chilled food?
content.explanation: Chilled food must be stored at or below 4 °C, with temperatures checked and logged twice per shift as stated in FSA-01 [§2.1].

content.question: Hot food held for service must be kept at or above 65 °C and discarded after 2 hours.
content.explanation: Hot food held for service must be kept at or above 65 °C and discarded after 2 hours according to FSA-01 [§2.3].

content.question: How long must food handlers wait before returning to work with food after experiencing symptoms of vomiting or diarrhoea?
content.explanation: Food handlers must report symptoms of vomiting or diarrhoea and must not work with food until 48 hours after symptoms stop, per FSA-01 [§4.1].

content.question: What are the four components of the CARE model used for handling guest complaints?
content.explanation: Complaints must be handled using the CARE model: Calm, Acknowledge, Resolve, Echo back as outlined in SOP-GR-01 [§2.1].

content.question: Within what timeframe must every complaint be logged in the Guest Incident Log?
content.explanation: Every complaint must be logged in the Guest Incident Log within 30 minutes, including the resolution offered, as specified in SOP-GR-01 [§2.3].

content.question: When must expense claims be submitted with original receipts?
content.explanation: Expense claims must be submitted with original receipts within 30 days of the expense as noted in FIN-01 [§4.2].

rubric.pass_condition: Achieves 100% accuracy on food safety quiz questions.
rubric.expected_performance: Accurately identifies temperature limits, allergen flags, and illness reporting rules.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly answers complaint escalation and CARE model questions.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates clear understanding of the CARE model and logging timeframes.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly identifies expense claim timelines and finance reconciliation requirements.
rubric.expected_performance: Shows awareness of finance expense rules and reconciliation deadlines.

modules.title: HR Operations
modules.purpose: To introduce F&B Associates to Aurelle Hotels & Residences HR operations, policies, working hours, leave entitlements, and compliance standards.
key_concepts: Absence reporting and sick leave documentation
Annual leave entitlements, notice, and blackout dates
assessment_topics: HR Operations and Policies Knowledge Check
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all learning activities, tasks, checklist items, and score at least 85% on the M05 quiz and assessment.

content.text: Understand working hours, overtime approval, shift policies, and absence reporting procedures.
Comply with annual leave request timelines, carry-forward rules, blackout dates, and medical certificate submissions.
Recognize obligations regarding conflict of interest declarations, 30-day check-ins, and mandatory assessment coaching reviews.

content.activity: Submit annual leave requests through the HR portal at least 14 days before leave begins
Declare any conflicts of interest, including family relationships with suppliers, to HR in writing
Submit a medical certificate within 48 hours of return for sick leave exceeding two consecutive days
Complete the 30-day check-in meeting with reporting manager and record it in the HR portal

content.description: Draft a formal written conflict of interest declaration notifying Human Resources of a family relationship with a supplier, following company guidelines.
content.expected_outcome: A complete and properly addressed conflict of interest declaration ready for submission to HR.
content.completion_criteria: The declaration clearly states the family relationship with the supplier and is formatted for HR submission.

content.situation: You are assigned to a night shift at Aurelle Penang Heritage. During your shift, you feel fatigued around 02:30 and want to take your break and step out to grab a snack from a nearby store outside the property.
expected_actions: Take your paid 30-minute break between 02:00 and 04:00.
Remain on the property during your break, as leaving the property is prohibited.

content.question: What is the standard working time per week at Aurelle Hotels & Residences?
content.explanation: Standard working time is 48 hours per week across six shifts; overtime is required to be approved in advance by the department head.

content.question: Employees working night shifts are permitted to leave the property during their paid 30-minute break between 02:00 and 04:00.
content.explanation: Employees working night shifts must take a paid 30-minute break between 02:00 and 04:00 and must not leave the property during it.

options: At least 30 minutes before the shift
At least 1 hour before the shift
At least two hours before the start of the shift
At any time before the shift ends
content.question: How far in advance must absence due to illness be reported to your supervisor?
content.explanation: Absence due to illness must be reported to the supervisor at least two hours before the start of the shift.

content.question: What is the annual leave entitlement for employees per year?
content.explanation: Employees are entitled to 30 calendar days of annual leave per year, accrued monthly from the date of joining.

options: Maximum of 5 days; excess lapses on 31 March
Maximum of 10 days; excess lapses on 31 December
Maximum of 5 days; excess lapses on 30 June
Maximum of 7 days; excess lapses on 31 March
content.question: How many unused annual leave days may be carried forward to the next year, and when do excess days lapse?
content.explanation: A maximum of 5 unused annual leave days may be carried forward to the next year; any excess days lapse on 31 March.

options: They are immediately terminated from employment
They must be referred to their manager for a coaching review before a third attempt
They are permanently barred from retaking the assessment
They must pay a re-testing fee
content.question: What happens if an employee fails a mandatory assessment twice?
content.explanation: Employees who fail a mandatory assessment twice must be referred to their manager for a coaching review before a third attempt.

content.topic: HR Operations and Policies Knowledge Check

rubric.expected_performance: Accurately answers questions related to standard shifts, overtime approvals, and illness notification timelines.

rubric.criterion: Comprehension of leave policies and compliance requirements
rubric.pass_condition: Score at least 30 out of 35 points in this section.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates knowledge of annual leave accrual, carry-forward rules, blackout dates, and medical certificate guidelines.

rubric.criterion: Knowledge of conduct policies and coaching procedures
rubric.pass_condition: Score at least 25 out of 30 points in this section.
rubric.expected_performance: Identifies correct procedures for conflict of interest declarations and assessment coaching reviews.

modules.title: In-Room Dining and 2 related areas
modules.purpose: To equip F&B Associates with essential knowledge and procedures for executing in-room dining service, handling incident reporting, security protocols, and compliance standards.
key_concepts: Operating Hours and Duty Manager Referrals
Knock, Announce, and Wait Entry Procedure
modules.completion_criteria: Complete all required checklists, tasks, role-play assessments, and achieve a minimum of 80% on the quiz within the designated timeframes.

content.text: Master in-room dining operational hours, verification procedures, and entry protocols.
Understand probation policies, security incident reporting, and injury escalation timeframes.

content.activity: Complete In-Room Dining Service training before your first room-service shift.

content.description: Perform corridor collection rounds to gather trays and trolleys placed outside guest rooms.
content.expected_outcome: All trays and trolleys placed in corridors are collected within 60 minutes of the guest placing them outside.
content.completion_criteria: Successfully clear and log all corridor trays within the required 60-minute window.

content.situation: You are preparing to deliver an in-room dining order to a guest room. You need to verify the guest and enter the room safely.
expected_actions: Confirm the guest's name against the room number in the PMS.
Ensure you do not announce the room number aloud in public areas.
Demonstrate the knock, announce and wait-for-invitation entry procedure.

content.question: When must an employee assigned to In-Room Dining complete their service training?
content.explanation: Employees assigned to In-Room Dining must complete In-Room Dining Service training before their first room-service shift.

options: Accept the order and prepare it anyway
Refer the order to the Duty Manager
Cancel the order without notifying anyone
Process it as a priority order
content.question: What must you do if a room-service order is requested outside the operating hours listed in Annex A?
content.explanation: Room-service orders may only be accepted during the operating hours listed for the property in Annex A; orders outside these hours must be referred to the Duty Manager.

options: The guest's name against the room number in the PMS
content.question: Before delivering an in-room dining order, what must the associate verify?
content.explanation: Before delivery, the associate must confirm the guest's name against the room number in the PMS and must not announce the room number aloud in public areas.

content.question: Within what timeframe must trays and trolleys placed in corridors be collected?
content.explanation: Trays and trolleys placed in corridors must be collected within 60 minutes of the guest placing them outside the room.

content.question: Who must any suspected security incident be reported to immediately?
content.explanation: Any suspected security incident must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately.

content.question: Within what timeframe must any injury to a guest or employee be reported to the Manager on Duty (MOD)?
content.explanation: Any injury to a guest or employee must be reported to the Manager on Duty (MOD) within 15 minutes.

rubric.pass_condition: Demonstrates flawless execution during the role-play assessment.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly verifies guest name in PMS without speaking room numbers aloud and successfully performs the knock, announce, and wait-for-invitation procedure.

rubric.pass_condition: Scores at least 80% on the module quiz.
rubric.expected_performance: Accurately identifies reporting channels and timelines for injuries, security incidents, and e-learning completion.

modules.title: Information Security
modules.purpose: To ensure all employees understand and practice essential information security, password standards, workstation safety, and acceptable IT usage.
key_concepts: IT acceptable use and MDM enrolment
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all e-learning modules, pass the quiz, and finish all Day 1 and Week 1 checklist and task requirements.

content.text: Complete Information Security e-learning and acknowledge policies within the required timeframe.
Apply password standards, multi-factor authentication, account sharing restrictions, and workstation locking rules.
Recognize phishing, protect guest privacy on social media, and adhere to IT acceptable use and device enrollment procedures.

content.activity: Acknowledge the Information Security Policy in the HR portal within your first week
Complete the Information Security Basics e-learning module before being granted system access
Enrol personal device in the Mobile Device Management app prior to connecting to staff Wi-Fi

content.description: Verify your system password meets the required standards and configure multi-factor authentication for your email and PMS accounts.
content.expected_outcome: Password is at least 12 characters long and MFA is active for email and PMS.
content.completion_criteria: Password confirmed to be >= 12 characters and MFA successfully set up.

content.situation: You need to step away from your workstation on the front desk to assist a guest across the room, leaving the PMS open on your screen.
expected_actions: Lock your workstation immediately before leaving it unattended.
Ensure no unauthorized individual can view or access your open sessions.

content.question: When must all employees acknowledge the Information Security Policy in the HR portal?
content.explanation: All employees must acknowledge the Information Security Policy in the HR portal within their first week.

content.question: You are permitted to post photographs of guest rooms and back-of-house areas on your personal social media.
content.explanation: Employees must not post photographs of guests, guest rooms or back-of-house areas on personal social media.

content.question: What is the minimum character length required for passwords?
content.explanation: Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.

options: Forward it to your colleagues to warn them
Report it using the Report Phishing button
Reply to the sender to verify authenticity
content.question: How should you handle a suspected phishing email?
content.explanation: Suspected phishing emails must be reported using the Report Phishing button and must not be forwarded to colleagues.

content.question: You can share your PMS login credentials with a coworker if they are helping you complete rush orders.
content.explanation: Users must never share login credentials; every action in the PMS must be performed under the user's own account.

options: Enrolment in the Mobile Device Management app
Written approval from the General Manager
Installation of hotel anti-virus software only
Nothing, staff Wi-Fi is open to all personal devices
content.question: What is required before connecting personal devices to the staff Wi-Fi?
content.explanation: Personal devices must not be connected to the staff Wi-Fi without enrolment in the Mobile Device Management app.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly identifies when training and acknowledgments are due.
rubric.expected_performance: Understands deadlines for policy acknowledgement and e-learning completion.

rubric.pass_condition: Answers password and account security rules without error.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates knowledge of password length, MFA requirements, and account uniqueness.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly states workstation locking and Wi-Fi connection rules.
rubric.expected_performance: Identifies proper workstation locking procedures and MDM enrolment rules for personal devices.

rubric.pass_condition: Chooses the Report Phishing button and avoids unauthorized social media posts.
rubric.expected_performance: Recognizes correct phishing reporting protocols and social media guest privacy restrictions.

modules.title: Payment & Cash Handling
modules.purpose: To ensure F&B Associates handle guest payments, cash floats, and card data securely and accurately according to company policies.
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all learning activities, pass the quiz with correct understanding of all requirements, and complete practical tasks including cash float sign-off.

content.text: Complete required payment card handling training and understand card data security rules.
Manage cash floats, pre-authorisations, and shift close counting procedures properly.
Identify and report cash variances and process refunds correctly.

content.activity: Complete Payment Card Handling training before operating a payment terminal or cash drawer
Sign for personal cash float at the start of the shift

content.description: Receive and sign for your personal cash float at the start of your shift, verifying it does not exceed USD 500 or local equivalent.
content.expected_outcome: Cash float is properly signed for and acknowledged before operating the cash drawer.
content.completion_criteria: Cash float sign-off sheet is completed and signed at the beginning of the shift.

content.situation: A guest paid for their dining bill using a credit card earlier today and is now requesting a refund. They ask you to hand them cash from the register for the refund.
expected_actions: Refuse to provide a cash refund for a card payment.
Explain that refunds must be processed to the original payment method.

options: Before operating a payment terminal or cash drawer
At the end of their probation period
content.question: When must an employee complete Payment Card Handling training?
content.explanation: Employees who process payments must complete Payment Card Handling training before operating a payment terminal or cash drawer.

content.question: Guest payment cards can be photocopied or written down if the guest gives explicit verbal permission.
content.explanation: Guest payment cards must never be photocopied, photographed or written down; card details are to be entered only into the payment terminal.

content.question: What is the maximum percentage allowed above the room rate when taking a pre-authorisation for incidentals?
content.explanation: Pre-authorisations must be taken through the terminal at check-in and must not exceed the room rate plus 20% for incidentals.

content.question: What is the maximum amount permitted for a personal cash float issued to a cashier?
content.explanation: Each cashier is issued a personal cash float, which must not exceed USD 500 or local equivalent, and must sign for it at the start of the shift.

content.question: Who must count the cash float at the end of every shift and where must the result be recorded?
content.explanation: At the end of every shift, the cash float must be counted by the cashier and a second employee and the result recorded on the Shift Close Form.

content.question: Cash variances greater than what amount must be reported to Finance on the same day?
content.explanation: Cash variances greater than USD 10 must be reported to Finance on the same day.

rubric.pass_condition: Demonstrates full compliance with card data protection rules.
rubric.expected_performance: Completed training prior to terminal operation and strictly enters card details into terminal without copying or photographing.

rubric.pass_condition: Successfully executes float sign-off and joint shift-close counting.
rubric.expected_performance: Signs for cash float at shift start, conducts end-of-shift count with a second employee, and fills out the Shift Close Form accurately.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately handles variance reporting thresholds and proper refund channels.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly identifies variances over USD 10 for same-day reporting to Finance and processes refunds to original payment methods.
